abstract: We prove an inhomogeneous Diophantine approximation theorem at log-squared smoothness. For every irrational $\theta$, real $\phi$, and fixed $\kappa>1/(16e^2)$, infinitely many integers $n$ have $P^+(n)\leq\kappa(\log n)^2$ and $\|\theta n+\phi\|<\exp(-c\log n/\log\log n)$ whenever $0<c<(1+\log(4\sqrt\kappa))/3$. The proof refines Baker's bilinear construction: a restricted divisor count removes its unspecified power loss, and the second saddle-point term supplies the endpoint margin. We also prove a finite Fourier bound for the canonical fractional Euler coefficients $\alpha(p^r)=(w_p)_r/r!$, uniformly for $0\leq w_p\leq1$ and arbitrary Mellin twists. A unique ordered factorization uses one shared beta variable at the crossing prime; its integrated square norm is bounded by one original counting mass. Exact Fourier separation retains sharp product caps. For a taper supported at $\kappa\log^2X$ and denominators $q^2=X\exp(d\log X/\log\log X)$, the resulting relative saving has exponent $(1+\log(2\sqrt\kappa)-3d)/4$. A bounded-variation continuum term can be included in this selected additive-frequency estimate. The estimate does not include the additive zero frequency or imply an RH criterion. Exact rational CPU controls verify the coefficient and cap identities. These are partial arithmetic results, with no new zero-free region or RH conclusion.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Submit the arithmetic result to the general community, as recommended by the RH-task review, without claiming an RH interface. Add Papers 115/v2 and 117/v1 and explicitly credit their ordered-crossing and exact sharp-cutoff separation devices. Remove the generic quadratic-defect display and undefined clock wording. The endpoint and coefficient theorems and proofs are unchanged.
title: Diophantine approximation at log-squared smoothness and fractional Euler coefficients
